<?php

function readTokens() {
    $input = file_get_contents('php://stdin');
    return preg_split('/\s+/', trim($input));
}

$tokens = readTokens();
$idx = 0;

function nextInt() {
    global $tokens, $idx;
    return intval($tokens[$idx++]);
}

$h1 = nextInt();
$h2 = nextInt();
$a = nextInt();
$b = nextInt();

$pos = $h1 + 8 * $a;
$dc = 0;
while (true) {
    if ($pos >= $h2) {
        echo $dc . "\n";
        exit;
    }
    if (12 * $a <= 12 * $b) {
        echo "-1\n";
        exit;
    }
    $pos -= 12 * $b;
    $pos += 12 * $a;
    $dc++;
}

<?php
function readIntArray() {
    $line = trim(fgets(STDIN));

    return array_map('intval', explode(' ', $line));

source_data.prob_desc_description: The 9-th grade student Gabriel noticed a caterpillar on a tree when walking around in a forest after the classes. The caterpillar was on the height h1 cm from the ground. On the height h2 cm (h2 > h1) on the same tree hung an apple and the caterpillar was crawling to the apple.Gabriel is interested when the caterpillar gets the apple. He noted that the caterpillar goes up by a cm per hour by day and slips down by b cm per hour by night.In how many days Gabriel should return to the forest to see the caterpillar get the apple. You can consider that the day starts at 10 am and finishes at 10 pm. Gabriel's classes finish at 2 pm. You can consider that Gabriel noticed the caterpillar just after the classes at 2 pm.Note that the forest is magic so the caterpillar can slip down under the ground and then lift to the apple.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print the only integer k — the number of days Gabriel should wait to return to the forest and see the caterpillar getting the apple. If the caterpillar can't get the apple print the only integer  - 1.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first line contains two integers h1, h2 (1 ≤ h1 < h2 ≤ 105) — the heights of the position of the caterpillar and the apple in centimeters. The second line contains two integers a, b (1 ≤ a, b ≤ 105) — the distance the caterpillar goes up by day and slips down by night, in centimeters per hour.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first example at 10 pm of the first day the caterpillar gets the height 26. At 10 am of the next day it slips down to the height 14. And finally at 6 pm of the same day the caterpillar gets the apple.Note that in the last example the caterpillar was slipping down under the ground and getting the apple on the next day.
